reader.requirement: At --std 85, END-REWRITE ends the scope of the REWRITE it closes (§1985:IV.6.4.3, IV.4.4.4): a delimited REWRITE is an imperative statement that may stand inside another statement's imperative phrase; the statements after END-REWRITE, and the containing statement's next phrase, belong to the containing statement; nested REWRITEs pair END-REWRITE with the innermost unterminated one; END-REWRITE may close a REWRITE written with no phrases; without END-REWRITE an unterminated REWRITE is conditional, which an imperative-statement slot refuses, and is ended implicitly by the containing statement's next phrase (ELSE) or the period. The 1985 format admits only REWRITE record-name-1 [FROM identifier-1] [INVALID KEY] [NOT INVALID KEY] [END-REWRITE], in that order.

reader.notes: The grammar ends rewriteStatement with END_REWRITE?, and ConditionalPhraseAssociation gives each phrase to the innermost unterminated statement, so END-REWRITE closes the innermost REWRITE and hands later phrases to the container. Every nesting shape behaved as the 1985 scope rules say. The edition switches on the path gate only the 2002 format elements around the statement, and each refused at 85.
